Asimov releases the open-source Menlo Python SDK

The SDK is public; the announced Edge source release remains separately unconfirmed.

Humanoids Daily ↗12 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Connecting applications to a robot

Menlo Research released Menlo SDK for Asimov 1. Python applications can issue walking and joint commands, read robot state, and access cameras and audio. The public repository uses Apache 2.0 and requires Python 3.12 or later.

Local and remote connections

LiveKit supports internet connections, while UDP serves local applications. The announcement demonstrates upper-body motions, VR teleoperation and a locomotion-policy loop that reads robot state and returns joint commands.

Control priority is not an emergency stop

The team also announced open-sourcing Asimov Edge, which arbitrates control sources; that source release remains unconfirmed in the reviewed evidence. Documentation gives Cockpit and gamepad priority over SDK applications and explicitly says the SDK is not an emergency stop.
